canonical_statement: For every class C of unary partial functions on Nat, if C contains a partial-recursive function and omits a partial-recursive function, then membership of eval c in C is not a computable predicate of the partial-recursive code c.
domain_and_universes: C : Set (Nat ->. Nat); f g : Nat ->. Nat; c : Nat.Partrec.Code; Prop in Lean universe 0
ordered_binders: positive represented witness f : Nat ->. Nat
negative represented witness g : Nat ->. Nat
hypotheses: exists f, Nat.Partrec f and f in C
exists g, Nat.Partrec g and g not in C
conclusion: Not (ComputablePred (fun c : Nat.Partrec.Code => Nat.Partrec.Code.eval c in C)).

killed: changed the semantic partial-function property to an intensional code property
changed the domain from partial functions to total functions

degenerate_cases: The empty and universal semantic classes are excluded by the two witness premises; kernel-checked lemmas show their induced predicates are computable. Witnesses must be represented by Nat.Partrec, so arbitrary non-enumerated partial functions cannot establish nontriviality.
alternate_encodings: The set formulation and predicate formulation are definitionally equivalent by the checked iff. Language recognizers and recursively enumerable sets remain uncredited without separate semantic transports.
status_boundary: This freezes and elaborates the exact intake-selected target with one pinned direct import, a checked set/predicate transport, four structural mutations, and two degenerate-property checks. It adds no new Rice-theorem proof and supplies no dependent-node evidence.
